起きて5分。まだ夢の途中。☀️

Five Minutes Awake, Still Half Dreaming.

秋の朝、寝癖も、散らかった部屋も、そのままで。

A quiet October morning in Japan.
No makeup. No perfect poses. Just a sleepy little moment.

※AI-generated fictional character

🔽日本語・画像生成プロンプト🔽
縦9:16、極めてフォトリアルなスマートフォン撮影風SNS日常写真。2026年10月中旬、朝7時半の日本の一般的なワンルームマンション。起床して5分ほどの23歳の架空の日本人成人女性が、乱れた白い布団の上に座り、眠そうな半目の表情で大きく背伸びしている。片腕を真上に伸ばし、もう片腕を頭の後ろに回す。黒に近いダークブラウンの無造作なミディアムヘア、寝癖、浮き毛、自然な左右非対称の顔、薄いクマ、毛穴や頬の赤みを残した素肌。健康的で自然な体型。服装は、前を開けたシワの多い白いオーバーサイズシャツ、胸元に繊細なレースと小さなリボンのあるくすみピンクの細ストラップ・リブキャミソール、アイボリーの短丈フリル付きラウンジショートパンツ。シャツは背伸びで自然に肩からずれ、リラックスした着崩れ感がある。片脚を前へ投げ出し、もう片脚を軽く曲げた無造作な座り姿勢。背景には白い壁、生成りのカーテン、観葉植物、木製の棚、マグカップ、充電ケーブル、生活用品、少し雑然とした普通の部屋。右側の窓から柔らかな秋の朝日が入り、明暗差と自然な影ができている。スマートフォンを棚に置いてセルフタイマーで撮ったような低めの目線、軽い広角感、わずかな暗部ノイズ。広告写真やグラビアではなく、飾らない日常の記録。過剰な美肌補正、スタジオ照明、不自然な体型、誘惑的なポーズ、文字、ロゴなし。

🔽English Image Generation Prompt🔽
Vertical 9:16, ultra-photorealistic candid smartphone photograph. Mid-October 2026, around 7:30 AM, inside an ordinary, slightly cluttered Japanese studio apartment. A fictional 23-year-old adult Japanese woman, awake for only five minutes, sits on an unmade bed and stretches sleepily. One arm reaches straight upward while the other rests behind her head. She has naturally messy, shoulder-length dark brown hair, flyaways, uneven bangs, sleepy half-open eyes, subtly puffy cheeks, faint under-eye shadows, realistic skin pores, and a completely natural, unretouched appearance. Healthy, realistic body proportions. She wears an oversized, wrinkled white button-down shirt left open and casually slipping off one shoulder, a dusty pink ribbed camisole with delicate lace trim, thin straps and a tiny bow, and very short ivory ruffled lounge shorts. The outfit feels feminine, slightly daring, yet believable as casual at-home sleepwear. Her legs rest in an asymmetrical, relaxed seated position, one extended toward the camera and the other loosely bent. The background includes rumpled white bedding, beige curtains, wooden shelving, small houseplants, mugs, charging cables, everyday household items, and the authentic imperfections of a modest Japanese apartment. Soft autumn morning sunlight enters through a window on the right, producing gentle shadows, slightly blown-out highlights and realistic indoor exposure. Low smartphone camera perspective, subtle wide-angle distortion, mild shadow noise, natural skin texture, imperfect candid framing. An intimate everyday morning moment, not a fashion editorial or glamour shoot. No artificial beauty filters, no exaggerated anatomy, no studio lighting, no seductive posing, no text, no logos.

Day 7 of teaching you how to create with AI.

The secret to cinematic AI videos isn't just the prompt. It's what happens BEFORE you generate your first shot. 🎬👀

Someone asked me yesterday how to create a good storyboard, so let's talk about it!

Whether you're creating a fashion film, product advert, UGC video, or AI movie, here's your simple roadmap. 👇

1️⃣ Start with the idea. Know what you want to create and the story you want to tell.

2️⃣ Structure your story. Give it a beginning, middle, and ending.

3️⃣ Break it into shots. Decide what happens in every scene and what your audience should see.

4️⃣ Direct the camera. Choose your angles, close-ups, camera movements, and transitions.

5️⃣ Upload your references to ChatGPT. Include your model, character, or product images and ask it to create a shot-by-shot storyboard.

6️⃣ Review before generating. Check the flow, character consistency, outfit details, and camera directions.

7️⃣ Bring it to life. Use your storyboard in Google Flow, generate your shots, and edit them together in CapCut.

Remember, a storyboard isn't just a collection of beautiful images. It's your visual roadmap!

Plan the story before you generate the scenes. That's how you gain more control over your AI videos. 🔥

💬 What's your biggest challenge: prompts, camera angles, character consistency, or video generation?

Tell me in the comments. Let's learn together! ❤️

I tried to explain Perturb in 90 seconds through one very small object: a sticker.

Researchers have shown that black-and-white stickers on a real stop sign can make a research classifier read it as a 45 mph speed limit. 

Put the same weakness in a warehouse robot's camera and the cost lands on three people: the operator (downtime), the maker (trust), whoever is standing nearby (risk). The warehouse in the video is a fictional scenario.

Perturb is the opposite bet: AI vs AI. On Bittensor Subnet 26, miners are paid to find the smallets change that flips a model's answer. Validators check that it flips and stays imperceptible. Copies earn nothing. 

The customer gets a robustness score, a heatmap, verified attack data for retraining and an on-chain certificate.

Live today: image-model testing. Robots, text, LLM and multimodal are future directions.

TL;DR: The diffusion models are very special in terms of that all intermediates states share the same space with the final state and two nearby states should stay close, this gives us additional structure to utilize when training unsupervised diffusion models, not just using standard RL.
